catalog_quote: El mazateco de Chiquihuitlán es una lengua tonal. En él existen cuatro niveles de tono y once deslices. Al escribirlo, generalmente no se hace ninguna marca para señalar los tonos. Pero cuando dos o más palabras tienen las mismas letras y únicamente se diferencian por el tono, entonces hay que señalar esa diferencia. ... 1.2.2.1. Las vocales acentuadas. En los casos en que una palabra difiere de otra sólo porque tiene un tono más alto, la palabra con el tono más alto debe llevar una vocal acentuada en la sílaba más fuerte. La sílaba más fuerte coincide con el tono más alto en la palabra. Cuando las sílabas de una palabra son igualmente altas, la primera es la de mayor fuerza. Ejemplos: cjín 'mucho' / cjin 'lejos'; cúya 'regreso' / cuya 'regresa (él)'; vitéxa 'mando' / vitexa 'manda (él)'; yungún 'uña' / yungun 'iglesia'; tsánga 'borrego' / tsanga 'algodón'; ndavá 'luz' / ndava 'su casa'.

tone_statements.translation: (1) bi-te-ch.á PV O-√Spec-√-PERS.HighTone 'I sweep'. In (1), bi- is analysed as the class-O inflectional prefix ..., in neutral aspect; the stem consists of a surface-specifying root -te- followed by a motion root chá, whose thematic vowel -a carries a toned person marker (HIGH tone). ... The other forms follow simple mechanisms: SUBJ 3, 6 bitecha takes the base theme, without tonal inflection, and serves as base for the three other plural persons
tone_statements.summary: Verb-morphology paper: Chiquihuitlán Mazatec 1SG is marked by a high tone on the thematic vowel (bitechá vs bitecha); negation involves 'modulation tonale'. No tone inventory; nothing on stress.

tone_statements.quote: ChM is a tone language. There are four level tones traditionally numbered from 1 (high, H) to 4 (low, L) through 2 (high mid, M⁺) and 3 (low mid, M) (Jamieson 1982); and tonal glides M/L-H/M⁺ (upglides) or the reverse (downglides). For greater ease of reading, we shall use accents in our transcriptions: e.g. á instead of a¹, a instead of a² or a³, à instead of a⁴, â for all downglides, and ă for all upglides. ... Tone patterns are thus a property of verb-forms. No lexical tone preassigned to roots need be assumed.

tone_statements.summary: Four level tones (1 H, 2 M+, 3 M, 4 L; Jamieson 1982) plus up/down glides written as level sequences; verb forms take tone patterns by tone-pattern class (A-D), 12 patterns listed; nothing on stress.

tone_statements.citation: Jamieson, Allan R. 1977. Chiquihuitlan Mazatec tone. In William R. Merrifield (ed.), Studies in Otomanguean phonology (SIL Publications in Linguistics 54), 107-136. Dallas: SIL & University of Texas at Arlington. ISBN 0-88312-067-4.
tone_statements.quote: Chiquihuitlán Mazatec¹ has four tones: high /1/, mid /2/, low-mid /3/, and low /4/. Contrast among the four tones is demonstrated in one-syllable words in isolation (1) and (2), in one-syllable words preceding a constant frame (3), in the final syllable of two-syllable words (4), and in the initial syllable of two-syllable words (5). ... A syllable may be realized with any one of the four tones or with a cluster of two or three tones. The tone clusters occurring in ChM are /14 24 34/, /11 21 31 41/, /114 214 314 414/, and /42 424/.
tone_statements.summary: Four level tones /1-4/ on each syllable plus two- and three-tone clusters realized as glides; tone sandhi rules across syllables, grammatical tone on verbs, automatic downdrift; nothing on stress.
